title: "4. Ideal patient"
---


::: {.cell}

:::


Eligibility criteria are the hardest part of a clinical trial to read: long inclusion and exclusion lists, often seemingly contradictory at first. [`04_ai_ideal_patient.R`](https://github.com/felippelazar/CancerTrialsBR/blob/main/R/04_ai_ideal_patient.R){target="_blank"} turns these criteria into a paragraph describing the patient who would fit the trial.

## The prompt

This is the longest prompt so far. Before writing, the model is told to organize the criteria by topic (diagnosis, prior treatments, performance status...) and cross-check inclusion against exclusion. That way, a criterion like "non-clear cell renal carcinoma" combined with excluding the papillary subtype becomes a single precise sentence.

The final text should have five sentences, start directly with the patient's characteristics and keep the exact medical terms. Lab tests and contraception requirements are left out unless essential.

```r
idealPatientPrompt <- "# Study Patient Profile Generator
## Task
You will receive a clinical studys eligibility criteria and generate a concise, flowing paragraph describing the ideal patient profile for this study in both English and Portuguese.

## Chain-of-Thought Process (Do Not Display in Output)
Before generating the final paragraphs, follow these analytical steps:

1. First, organize all eligibility criteria into categorical groups:
   - Primary diagnosis (disease type, stage, classification)
   - Prior treatments (medications, procedures, therapies)
   - Performance status requirements
   - Exclusion criteria
   # ...
2. Identify and reconcile any complementary or contradictory criteria
3. Prioritize the most clinically relevant aspects
4. Draft and refine 5 comprehensive sentences that capture the essence of the eligible patient

## Requirements for the Patient Profile
# ... (12 rules, see the script)

{{
  \"ideal_patient_english\": \"Your 5-sentence English paragraph here\",
  \"ideal_patient_portuguese\": \"Your 5-sentence Portuguese paragraph here\"
}}

The study eligibility criteria are: {var_1}."
```

## Applying it to each trial

Only one variable is sent here: the full eligibility criteria.

```r
df_studies <- fromJSON('data/out_03_studies.json')

df_studies %>%
      split(1:nrow(.)) %>%
      pblapply(function(x) chatLLM(x, intruction_prompt = idealPatientPrompt,
                                   var_1 = x[['study_elegibility_criteria']])) %>%
      do.call(dplyr::bind_rows, .) %>%
      toJSON(pretty = TRUE) %>%
      write(file = 'data/out_04_studies.json')
```

## Result

Look at the difference in length between the original criteria and the paragraph generated for the first trial. The criteria have 2,594 characters; the paragraph, 1401.

>  Adult with previously untreated, histologically documented unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction, or distal third of the esophagus, demonstrating positive CLDN18.2 expression by central IHC testing. Patient must have a confirmed PD-L1 CPS status by central IHC, with cohort assignment based on PD-L1 positivity and investigator-assessed eligibility for immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. ECOG performance status must be 0 or 1 without deterioration in the two weeks prior to screening and randomization, and the patient should have a minimum life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and a body weight of 35 kg or more. Exclusion applies to those with known HER2-positive status, significant or unstable gastric bleeding or untreated ulcers, active or history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders requiring systemic immunosuppression, CNS pathology, clinically significant or drain-dependent pleural effusions or ascites, need for parenteral nutrition due to obstruction, peripheral neuropathy ≥ CTCAE Grade 2, persistent toxicities from prior anticancer therapy (except alopecia), cardiac abnormalities, uncontrolled diabetes or diabetic neuropathy within 3 months, active or uncontrolled hepatitis A, B, or C, uncontrolled HIV, or known DPD enzyme deficiency. At least one lesion must be present and assessable by RECIST 1.1 criteria.
